question.text: What is the difference between Customer Due Diligence (CDD) and Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD)?

answer.text: CDD involves standard identity verification and risk assessment, while EDD requires additional measures such as verifying source of wealth, obtaining senior management approval, and enhanced monitoring for higher-risk customers
CDD is performed only for individual customers, while EDD is performed only for corporate customers
CDD requires physical document verification, while EDD only requires electronic verification
CDD is mandatory for all customers, while EDD is optional and depends on the reporting entity's discretion

explanation.text: The Logic: CDD is the baseline level of due diligence applied to all customers, involving identity verification and understanding business purpose (p.96). EDD goes beyond CDD and is required for higher-risk scenarios — pages 103-104 list additional measures such as verifying source of wealth and funds, obtaining senior management approval, and conducting enhanced ongoing monitoring. The Trap: Option D is dangerous — EDD is not optional. It is mandatory when risk indicators warrant it, such as for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, or complex/unusual transactions. Option C (physical vs electronic verification) is a distractor unrelated to the CDD/EDD distinction. Note: Apply EDD whenever you encounter PEPs, customers from high-risk jurisdictions, complex ownership structures, or unusually large/complex transactions — failing to do so is a compliance violation under IFSCA KYC norms.
